title: Residensi Dutamas Dahlia: a RM300,000 home in a RM1 million area.
excerpt: A freehold Rumawip project in residential Dutamas, sold at RM300,000 plus a RM30,000 renovation package. Sean rates the build quality and facilities above many open-market projects, but notes highway noise and congestion.
takeaways: 900 sq ft three-bedroom units at RM300,000, with a compulsory RM30,000 kitchen and renovation package.
Four lifts for 12 units a floor, 1.78 m corridors, a transfer plate and a 35 to 40 m infinity pool.
Next to the NKVE toll, a dead-end road and an abandoned project, on a congested route.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: Dutamas Dahlia is a freehold Rumawip project by a relatively new developer. Buyers paid about RM300,000 for a 900 sq ft unit plus a RM30,000 renovation package covering soft-closing kitchen cabinets. Each floor has 12 units, served by three passenger lifts and a service lift, along 1.78 m corridors where no doors face each other. A transfer plate keeps the facilities deck clear for a long infinity-edge lap pool, a wading pool, a gym, a reading room, a covered playground and a barbecue area, and the split-level car park is left exposed to show off tidy concrete work.

Sean viewed a three-bedroom, two-bathroom corner unit with a 3.1 m-wide living room, a kitchen long enough to add an island, a yard with a window, and a master bedroom with two windows and a hill view. Fittings are simpler, with smaller tiles, one socket per room and steel railings.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: The project sits on the residential side of Dutamas off Jalan Dutamas Raya, beside the NKVE toll and near a French international school, with the luxury Alex Residences opposite. Mont Kiara, Publika, the courts, MITEC, the MRT3 line and offices along Jalan Segambut are close, and new links to Jalan Kuching are being upgraded. An abandoned project and an empty plot stand nearby, and the main road is often congested.

sections.heading: Rent and returns
paragraphs: Buyers paid about RM300,000 plus the RM30,000 package, while three-bedroom units nearby average about RM700,000 to RM800,000 and some exceed RM1 million. Units had only just been handed over, so there were no rental figures yet.

standout.title: Nothing hidden in the car park
standout.body: The car park and parts of the deck are left without false ceilings, with flat slabs and pipes neatly exposed. Sean reads it as confidence in the build: most developers cover up the concrete, but here the clean formwork lines and tidy services are on show, and leaks are easy to reach.

pros: Dutamas: three-bedroom units nearby sell for about RM700,000 to over RM1 million, reflecting the connectivity, Mont Kiara catchment, courts, Publika, MRT3 and improving roads to Jalan Kuching.
Workmanship, design and facilities: a pool, equipped gym, play areas and landscaping done with pride, which he thinks should become the standard for all Rumawip projects.
The common areas: wide corridors, four lifts for 12 units, a 3.1 m-wide living room, a transfer plate, tidy services and landscaping even on the car park.
cons: The micro setting: beside the highway and a dead end that will serve future projects, with construction traffic for years, though the windows block sound well.
Design quirks: a staircase right off the drop-off and a split-level car park that takes long to climb, while some may dislike the exposed ceilings.
Supply and congestion: everyone wants this area, so peak-hour jams come with it, and the compulsory RM30,000 renovation fee remains debatable.

closing: Excellent value and build quality for eligible buyers, good for own stay and for renting out.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this October 2025 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. An owner let Sean view the unit just after handover; prices are as the owner and Sean quoted them. Rumawip eligibility, resale and rental rules vary, so check them before buying.
